newsitem.title: USA: Women pass 10 percent mark on Fortune 500 boards.
newsitem.headline: Women pass 10 percent mark on Fortune 500 boards.

text.p: Women held 10.2 percent of seats on boards of Fortune 500 companies in 1996, breaking through the 10 percent barrier for the first time, according to Catalyst, a research and advisory organisation.
However, among inside directors, or executives on their own company's board of directors, only 11 out of 1,216 -- 0.9 percent -- are women.
The results were published in the "1996 Catalyst Census of Women Board Directors of the Fortune 500," made available Wednesday.
Women on Fortune 500 boards rose from 9.5 percent in 1995, 8.7 percent in 1994 and 8.3 percent in 1993.
Catalyst found that 83 percent of Fortune 500 companies have one or more women directors, up from 69 percent in 1993, the year New York-based Catalyst began publishing the census.
Minority women represent 12.6 percent of women board directors, holding 1.4 percent ot total board seats.

The industry with the highest percentage of board seats held by women was soaps and cosmetics, at 19 percent. Women hold 17 percent of board seats in publishing and printing, and 15 percent in savings institutions. On the low end, only 3 percent of board seats are held by women in the mail, package, freight delivery industry and 5.5 percent in railroads.

Comparing data with another study, the "1996 Catalyst Census of Women Corporate Officers and Top Earners," Catalyst found a significant correlation between the number of women board directors and women corporate officers.

Currently, only 57 women hold positions of the highest rank in Fortune 500 companies, compared with 2,373 men. These women represent 2.4 percent of those holding the title chairman, vice chairman, president, chief executive officer, chief operating officer or executive vice president, Catalyst said.
